newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/ADT busy on takeover, calls pop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/ADT busy on takeover, calls pop.

text.p: Trading in options on U.S.-traded shares of ADT Ltd increased Wednesday after the company received a buyout offer, but more notable were some of the price changes in the options.
The biggest concentration of activity was in the December 17-1/2, 20 and 22-1/2 calls, which expire on Friday. More than 9,000 contracts traded between those three options.
The December 20 call rose 1,050 percent, or 2-5/8 points, to 2-7/8. The December 22-1/2 call rose 600 percent.
ADT shares in the U.S. were up three at 23-1/8 in late trade on consolidated volume of more than 7.3 million shares.
The electronic security firm received a buyout offer Wednesday from Western Resources Inc for $22.50 per ADT share.
The Western Resources offer comes after Republic Industries Inc's $5 billion bid to take over ADT failed in September.
That bid was terminated because of a sharp drop in Republic's share price that lowered the value of the proposed merger.
ADT said Wednesday it would review Western's unsolicited $3.5 billion offer. Western holds 27 percent of ADT.
Traders said options investors were buying and selling ADT calls, with some bias in pricing indicating expectations that the stock would climb or that a higher bid would emerge.
In addition, the stock's ability to climb over the $22.50 offering price indicated that stock investors also expected a higher bid, they said.
Western Resources options, which trade on the CBOE and the American Stock Exchange, saw limited action.
